title: UniVer: A Unified Perspective for Multi-step and Multi-draft Speculative Decoding
claim: Prior verification optimizes only the horizontal or only the vertical dimension of a candidate tree; ours jointly optimizes both.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right, shared layer labels, grayed-out ignored nodes in priors
description: Three side-by-side panels show the same layered candidate tree (Layer 0 to Layer 3) under different verification paradigms. Panel (a), blue, shows multi-draft horizontal OT: only the Layer 1 siblings are highlighted, and deeper layers are grayed out with the label 'Vertically Myopic: Ignores hierarchical dependency.' Panel (b), orange, shows multi-step sequence-level verification: only a single vertical chain is highlighted, and the other branches are faded, labeled 'Horizontally limited: Relies on local heuristics.' Panel (c), in green, shows UniVer: every layer is highlighted with shaded bands. Intra-layer mass allocation is marked at the top, and green down arrows mark inter-layer mass propagation. Each panel has a rounded title box in a matching color, and the captions are below. The eye goes first to the colored highlights, then to the contrast with the faded nodes.
caption: Conceptual illustration of verification paradigms. (a) Multi-Draft approaches (e.g., [ref]) optimize horizontal selection via OT but ignore vertical dependencies (vertically myopic). (b) Multi-Step approaches (e.g., Traversal Verification [ref]) optimize vertical acceptance but rely on local heuristics for horizontal selection (horizontally limited). (c) UniVer unifies both dimensions via Conditional OT, enabling parallel intra-layer mass allocation for different branches and seamless inter-layer mass propagation.
abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates Large Language Models via draft-then-verify, where verification can be framed as an Optimal Transport (OT) problem. Existing approaches typically handle multi-draft and multi-step aspects in isolation, applying either flat OT to single-step drafts or per-token rejection sampling to tree-structured candidates. This separation leaves the joint regime (where multi-step dependencies meet multi-draft branching) poorly optimized, as local verification rules fail to exploit the coupling between horizontal and vertical dimensions of candidate trees. In this paper, we propose a unified perspective that casts tree-based verification as a conditional OT problem. Our key insight is that vertical dependencies can be abstracted through prefix acceptance probabilities, which act as dynamic scaling factors to actively guide horizontal draft selection. Based on this principle, we introduce UniVer, a verification algorithm that jointly optimizes across tree levels by composing local optimal transport plans under prefix constraints. We prove that UniVer remains lossless and achieves the optimal acceptance rate under the proposed conditional framework. Extensive experiments across different tasks and models demonstrate that UniVer improves acceptance length by 4.2% to 8.5% over standard recursive rejection sampling without replacement, while maintaining exact distributional alignment with the target model.
